text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London stepped back from an early uptrend to finish at the day's lows on aggressive trade selling towards the close, traders said. September and November led the decline, each losing $23 to end at $1,597 and $1,587 per tonne respectively. No fresh fund or speculative involvement was seen. Technically the market might rise slightly if September regained its grip above the 5-day moving average of $1,697, analysts said. There was no fresh news and weather services said no damaging cold was in sight the next days in Brazilian coffee areas.

Arabica futures in New York ended the day weaker in an uneventful session, in what traders said was mainly a local dominated market. Benchmark September lost 1.50 cents/lb on the day ending at 160.45 cents/lb, after ranging between 163.50 and 159.00 cents/lb. Spot July, which expires on Monday, fell 0.35 cents/lb to 186.90 cents/lb, while the outer months closed down 0.25 to 1.45 cents/lb. The July/September switch widened to 26.45 cents/lb compared with 25.75 cents at the close on Wednesday, while the September/December switch narrowed to 12.85 cents/lb from 13.20 cents/lb. Technically, traders said September still faced support at 155.00 cents/lb, with the next level seen at 150.00 cents/lb. Resistance was seen near 165.00 cents/lb. FUNDAMENTALS
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported that certified coffee stocks rose by 1,737 60-kg bags as of July 16, to 77,151 bags. An additional 36,587 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

MAN - World consumer coffee stocks stood at 10.9 million 60- kg bags in May, up from 9.9 million in April and 9.1 million in May 1996, UK trade house E.D.& F. Man said in its latest report. Stocks in Europe rose to 7.6 million bags from 6.8 million in April and 5.8 million in April 1996. US stocks rose to 1.97 million bags in May from 1.85 million in April, but were 294,000 bags lower than in May 1996. Stocks in Japan were also higher at 1.24 million bags, up by 319,000 bags year on year. Man said US certified coffee stocks had started to increase in early July as coffee has been attracted to the terminal by the 20 cents/lb premium for the July contract against September.

PHILIPPINES ** - Philippine coffee exports in February 1997 amounted to 3,000 bags which brought cumulative exports in October/February 1996/97 up to 11,600 bags compared to 5,600 bags in the like period the previous year. Total exports in October/September 1995/96 were 23,000 bags. The major country of destination for Philippine green coffee was Singapore with 10,700, up from 4,000 bags.

TURKEY ** - Coffee imports in August 1996 reached 13,400 bags which brought cumulative imports in the first 8 months of 1996 (January/August) up to 220,900 bags against 120,700 bags in 1995. Total imports in 1995 amounted to 184,200 bags, up from 133,200 bags in 1994. The major supplier of green coffee in 1996 was Brazil with 184,000 vs 92,800 bags.
